newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 15.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page:

WASHINGTON - President Clinton prepared to announce U.S. willingness to participate in a new international peacekeeping force in Bosnia, a step that would reverse a longstanding commitment to bring U.S. troops home from the Balkans within about one year.

WASHINGTON - U.S. troops bound for Zaire as part of an international military mission to aid starving Rwandan refugees are likely to enter the area without a formal ceasefire among warring tribal factions there.

WASHINGTON - After hundreds of millions of dollars in campaign spending, countless news stories, three debates and hours of advertising, Americans knew no more about how the two major presidential candidates stood on key issues when they voted than they did when the fall campaign began in September, according to a survey.

BALTIMORE - Civil liberties lawyers asked for a $250,000 contempt-of-court fine against the Maryland State Police, saying troopers still are conducting disproportionate numbers of drug searches of cars driven by African Americans two years after agreeing to stop.
WASHINGTON - Cardinal Joseph Bernardin, the Roman Catholic archbishop of Chicago, died of pancreatic cancer.
WASHINGTON - Because of crushing demand for new telephone numbers, Northern Virginia residents will be getting another area code beginning in late 1999, according to Bell Atlantic Corp.
